title: Stealth aircraft: public RCS evidence
subtitle: Public evidence and its limits
purpose: This page helps readers with radar knowledge assess public RCS claims about the F-117, F-22, F-35 and B-2. It shows each claim with its evidence and the limits of that evidence.
scope_notes: This page does not rank the aircraft.
This page does not give an RCS value for a service aircraft.
A photograph or an outline does not give RCS. A model curve does not give the RCS of an aircraft.

evidence_types.label: Aircraft measurement
evidence_types.rule: Identify the actual test aircraft and configuration. Keep disclosed measurements apart from an account of tests without results.

evidence_types.label: Physical model measurement
evidence_types.rule: Identify the material, size, scale and represented features where the source states them.

evidence_types.label: Simulation
evidence_types.rule: Identify the model, its assumptions and the effects that it leaves out.

evidence_types.label: Manufacturer claim
evidence_types.rule: Identify the manufacturer. A reported test does not disclose the results that it does not give.

evidence_types.label: Official qualitative account
evidence_types.rule: Other public claim: an official account in words, not in numbers. Identify the original claim and its source.

evidence_types.label: Public numerical assertion
evidence_types.rule: Other public claim: a number that a public source states. Identify the original claim and its source.

results.label: Supported within stated limits
results.rule: The evidence supports the exact claim within the scope that the page shows.

results.label: Contradicted by comparable evidence
results.rule: Comparable evidence conflicts with a documented claim. The page states the conflict and the conditions.

results.label: Cannot verify from public evidence
results.rule: The values, the conditions or suitable evidence are not available in public.

disclosure_levels.label: Account of tests: no results disclosed
Curves in printed figures: no raw data found

aircraft.name: F-117
aircraft.summary: A single-seat attack aircraft with a faceted shape. The Air Force attributes its reduced RCS to the shape and a coating. A NASA-funded study measured an aluminum model.

design_features.evidence_limit: Attributed by the Air Force. No source here gives its separate effect.
Attributed by the Air Force. No source here gives its separate effect.

aircraft.name: F-22
aircraft.variant_reason: The cited sources say F-22 and do not name a variant.
aircraft.summary: A fighter that carries its missiles in an internal weapons bay. A 1998 GAO report describes radar tests of a full-scale F-22 on a pole. The report gives no results.

design_features.evidence_limit: GAO states that external weapons increase RCS. It gives no size of the effect.

aircraft.name: F-35
aircraft.variant_reason: The photograph caption, the design account and the simulation do not name one variant. The SigMA release concerns the F-35C.
aircraft.summary: A fighter family with three variants. Lockheed Martin attributes its stealth to aligned edges, embedded sensors and internal carriage. A company test account gives no numeric results.

design_features.evidence_limit: Manufacturer account. No independent measurement of the effect.
Manufacturer account. No independent measurement of the effect.

design_features.feature: Internal carriage of weapons and fuel
design_features.evidence_limit: Manufacturer account. No independent measurement of the effect.

aircraft.name: B-2
aircraft.variant_reason: The fact sheet, the GAO report and the photograph caption say B-2 and do not name a variant.
aircraft.summary: A flying-wing bomber. The Air Force names its shape, composite materials and coatings as parts of its low observability. GAO limits what the early radar tests show.

design_features.evidence_limit: Attributed by the Air Force. No source here gives its separate effect.

claims.title: Shape and coating
claims.claim: The Air Force attributes reduced F-117 RCS to its faceted shape and coating.
claims.grounds: Its public account identifies both features.
claims.warrant: This source supports the attributed qualitative account of the design.
claims.backing: AFMC account, paragraph about shape and coating.
claims.qualifier: The support concerns the qualitative account. The source does not quantify individual effects.
claims.rebuttal: Photographs alone cannot verify those effects under radar test conditions.
claims.assessed_scope: The attribution in the Air Force account. Not the size of any effect.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer a numeric reduction or an aircraft ranking.
claims.conditions_not_stated: No measurement. Frequency, aspect, polarization and test conditions are not stated.

sources.locator: Paragraph 4, the paragraph about shape and coating
sources.quote: While not invisible to radar, the Nighthawk's distinctive, faceted shape and a special low observable coating combined to greatly reduce its radar cross section and any adversary's ability to target it.

claims.title: Model response
claims.claim: The NASA study compares measured and reconstructed responses from an F-117 model.
claims.grounds: The report identifies the model and separates the traces.
claims.warrant: This evidence supports a comparison within the model study.
claims.qualifier: The result concerns a model. Its magnitude does not establish absolute aircraft RCS.
claims.rebuttal: Transfer requires evidence for model fidelity and calibration.
claims.assessed_scope: The comparison of original and reconstructed curves for one aluminum model in one report. Not the service aircraft.
claims.conditions_not_stated: Polarization, magnitude reference, calibration and experimental uncertainty are not stated.

sources.locator: Section 5.1, printed page 76 (PDF page 86). Figures 5.7–5.12, printed pages 84–89 (PDF pages 94–99).
sources.quote: The model is made of aluminum sheets. It is about 5½ feet long and 4 feet wide.

claims.title: Internal stores
claims.claim: GAO links internal F-22 stores to its low radar signature.
claims.grounds: The report describes internal stores and states that external stores increase RCS.
claims.warrant: The source supports a qualitative comparison of these configurations.
claims.qualifier: The source does not quantify the benefit for stated radar conditions.
claims.rebuttal: The effect depends on the stores and test conditions.
claims.assessed_scope: The qualitative statement about internal and external weapons in a 1998 report. Not a measured difference.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer equivalence across store configurations.
claims.conditions_not_stated: Radar conditions, the stores and the size of the effect are not stated.

sources.quote: Payload is a key parameter because the F-22 is designed to carry missiles in its internal weapons bay, not externally. Carrying weapons externally increases an aircraft’s radar cross section and can allow easier detection by enemy radar.

claims.title: Full-scale tests
claims.claim: GAO documents full-scale F-22 pole tests in its 1998 report.
claims.grounds: The report describes tests with an F-22 on a pole.
claims.warrant: This evidence supports the existence of the reported programme.
claims.qualifier: The cited account does not disclose numeric results with complete conditions.
claims.rebuttal: A test programme can possess data that its public report does not release.
claims.assessed_scope: The existence of the pole tests that GAO described in March 1998, during development. Not a current service configuration.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer numeric RCS or a current service configuration.
claims.conditions_not_stated: Results, frequency, aspect, polarization and configuration are not disclosed.

sources.locator: Appendix I, Radar Cross Section, printed pages 17–18. Also Low Observability, printed page 20.
sources.quote: RCS design validation and specification compliance are also being conducted with a full-scale F-22 mounted on a pole enabling testers to take RCS measurements. This testing will continue into 1999.

claims.title: Public design account
claims.claim: Lockheed Martin attributes F-35 stealth to aligned edges, embedded sensors, and internal weapons and fuel.
claims.grounds: The manufacturer identifies these features in its public description.
claims.warrant: The description supports attribution of this design account to the manufacturer.
claims.backing: F-35 design account, paragraph about stealth features.
claims.qualifier: This manufacturer account does not independently establish the contribution of each feature.
claims.rebuttal: A stated mechanism does not establish its measured magnitude on an aircraft.
claims.assessed_scope: The attribution in the manufacturer account. The account also names reduced engine signature, which the claim leaves out.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer independent quantitative verification.
claims.conditions_not_stated: The size of each contribution and any test conditions are not stated.

sources.locator: Section “More Than Meets the Eye”, paragraph 2
sources.quote: Aligned edges, reduced engine signature, embedded sensors, and internal carriage of weapons and fuel all contribute to the F-35's stealth.

claims.title: Signature after damage
claims.claim: The SigMA model retained its stealth signature after surface damage.
claims.grounds: Lockheed Martin reports baseline and damaged-model measurements and states that the signature remained intact.
claims.warrant: Independent verification requires the values and relevant test conditions.
claims.backing: F-35C test account, paragraphs about SigMA.
claims.qualifier: The account does not disclose numeric results or complete radar conditions.
claims.rebuttal: A valid development test can lack enough public evidence for independent verification.
claims.assessed_scope: Performance after damage, as the 2008 release reports it. The page cannot check it.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer a stated numeric RCS.
claims.conditions_not_stated: Numeric results, frequency, aspect, polarization and the details of the damage are not disclosed.

sources.quote: After obtaining baseline radar cross section (RCS) measurements from a highly detailed, full-scale Signature Measurement Aircraft (SigMA), a team of Lockheed Martin and Northrop Grumman engineers intentionally inflicted extensive damage -- more than three dozen significant defects -- on the model. The damage represented the cumulative effect of more than 600 flight hours of military aircraft operations. RCS measurements taken after the damage showed that the stealthy signature remained intact.

claims.title: Shape and materials
claims.claim: The Air Force identifies the B-2's shape, composite materials, and coatings as contributors to low observability.
claims.grounds: Its fact sheet lists these features.
claims.warrant: The source supports the attributed qualitative account of the design.
claims.backing: B-2 fact sheet, paragraph about low-observability processes.
claims.qualifier: Low observability includes more than radar signature. The source does not quantify individual effects.
claims.rebuttal: The visible shape alone cannot establish the complete aircraft's RCS.
claims.assessed_scope: The attribution in the Air Force fact sheet. Not the size of any effect.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer a numeric RCS.
claims.conditions_not_stated: The size of each effect and any radar conditions are not stated.

sources.locator: Features, paragraph 3, the paragraph about low-observability processes
sources.quote: The B-2's low observability is derived from a combination of reduced infrared, acoustic, electromagnetic, visual and radar signatures. These signatures make it difficult for the sophisticated defensive systems to detect, track and engage the B-2. Many aspects of the low-observability process remain classified; however, the B-2's composite materials, special coatings and flying-wing design all contribute to its "stealthiness."

claims.title: Scope of early tests
claims.claim: GAO states that the early B-2 tests did not represent operational conditions or long-term wear and maintenance.
claims.grounds: The report identifies these limits of the initial programme.
claims.warrant: These exclusions limit the conclusions that the tests support.
claims.qualifier: This assessment concerns the initial programme, not every later B-2 test.
claims.rebuttal: Later tests might address these factors. Assess their sources separately.
claims.assessed_scope: The early Block 2 flight tests of the first B-2 development aircraft, as GAO described them in April 1991.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer the radar signature after operational wear.
claims.conditions_not_stated: Numeric results and test frequencies are not disclosed. This page does not assess later tests.

sources.locator: Results in Brief, printed page 5 (context on printed pages 4–6)
sources.quote: The early Block 2 tests were initial development tests and were not designed to demonstrate the B-2’s full capabilities or test the B-2 in a representative operational environment. In addition, the tests did not attempt to account for the effects of day-to-day operations, wear and tear on the aircraft and equipment, or maintenance over a long time frame.

other_numerical_evidence.stated_conditions: Model 79 cm × 118 cm. POSTECH compact range. 8.3–12.3 GHz. Aspect ±4.8° about the nose. Vertical polarization. The figures concern ISAR images and extracted scattering centres.
other_numerical_evidence.conditions_status: These conditions come from the page specification. The page could not open the article on 2026-10-03 to check them again.
other_numerical_evidence.reason: Indexed PDF text indicates KOGL Type 4, but the direct download failed. Crossref lists Wiley terms. The exact terms are not verified, so the page does not copy any curve.

other_numerical_evidence.stated_conditions: Monostatic simulation with POFACETS v4.5. Frequencies 0.3, 1 and 10 GHz. Incident TM polarization. Azimuth 0–180° in steps of 0.1°. θ = 120–122° in its coordinates. The model has no RAM, no diffraction and no multiple reflections.
other_numerical_evidence.conditions_status: Checked against an archived copy of the paper on 2026-10-03.
other_numerical_evidence.author_limit_quote: It is, however, worth underscoring that the RCS is evaluated without accounting for RAM covering the F-35 surface.
other_numerical_evidence.reason: Its first page says: “© 2024 IEEE. Personal use is permitted, but republication/redistribution requires IEEE permission.” The page has no such permission, so it does not copy any curve.

no_curve_reasons.F22: No checked public source gives an F-22 curve. GAO describes pole tests but releases no results.
no_curve_reasons.F35: The checked F-35 simulation curve needs IEEE permission to republish. The page has no permission, so it shows only the record and the link.
no_curve_reasons.B2: No checked public source gives a B-2 curve. GAO describes early flight tests but releases no values.

search_limit: The checked sources do not give comparable curves for all 4 service aircraft. This result of a limited search does not prove that no public dataset exists.
